clue.text: Part of garden in which everything is easy

definitions.meaning: a planted patch of a garden given over to one kind of flowering shrub
an idiom for a comfortable, trouble-free situation

explanation.surface: A gardener describes the one plot that needs no work.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a flowerbed of one shrub; figuratively a life of comfort, as in the saying that life is not one.

clue.text: A lot of money laid out on Oriental dessert

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another goes above it

parts.words: A lot of money laid out
parts.note: to spend a bomb is British slang for spending a great deal of money
E is the abbreviation for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: Someone splashes out a fortune on a fancy Eastern pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oriental' looks like part of the definition but gives E; the dessert is a moulded frozen one.
explanation.definitionFit: A moulded frozen pudding, often ice cream layered in a dome, is a classic French dessert of this name.

clue.text: I'm annoyed — are you?

definitions.meaning: said sharply as an exclamation, the phrase protests at someone's behaviour
asked politely, the phrase enquires whether the other person objects

explanation.surface: One speaker snaps at another and asks whether they too are cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The same three-word phrase is an indignant protest when exclaimed and a courteous request for permission when asked.

clue.text: Global? Precisely!

definitions.meaning: an idiom meaning exactly, as in looking exactly like someone

explanation.surface: A terse exchange: one word offered, another confirming it exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means spanning the whole earth; idiomatically it means exactly or in every respect.

clue.text: I owe £3, roughly, for the rig needed here

indicators.note: done roughly, the letters are put together in no careful order

parts.note: the pound sign is L (libra), so three pounds gives three Ls

explanation.surface: Someone owes a few pounds for hiring some gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped the pound sign; the page prints '£3'. 'Roughly' rearranges I OWE with LLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A drilling rig is set up over a bore sunk to extract petroleum.

clue.text: Former player becomes debt-collector

parts.note: EX is a prefix meaning former
an actor plays a part on stage

explanation.surface: A retired performer takes up debt collecting.
explanation.definitionFit: One who exacts payment demands money owed, as a collector of debts does.

clue.text: Mug draws back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for draws from right to left

parts.note: to tow is to draw or pull along

explanation.surface: A drinking vessel being pulled backwards across a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' is not a cup here but the British verb to mug up, study hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug up is British slang for cramming study, which is just what a studious pupil does.

clue.text: I pulled up outside — how strange!

indicators.note: outside says the turned word for pulled goes round I
in a down clue, up means the word for pulled is read from the bottom

parts.note: drew is the past tense of draw, to pull

explanation.surface: Someone stopped the car outside and found it odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DREW into WERD, which goes 'outside' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd and uncanny things are eerie or bizarre, a synonym for strange.

clue.text: Article on fawns inspires revulsion

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another goes above it

parts.note: the definite article
to fawn is to creep, toady servilely

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about young deer makes readers recoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fawns' looks like young deer but is the verb, toadies.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom names a shuddering feeling of disgust or unease, as when something gives you shivers.

clue.text: Themes once, twice, rehashed, make an appearance

indicators.note: rehashed material is reworked into new form, so these letters are rearranged
twice tells us to use the word once two times over

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Old themes are recycled again and again until they turn up anew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles ONCE, and 'rehashed' scrambles THEMES with ONCEONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive or emerge into view is to appear, an idiom for turning up.

clue.text: Springtime examination of chief officer

parts.note: May is a month of spring
an oral is a spoken test

explanation.surface: A town's top official sits a test in May.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a mayor, the civic head of a town, this adjective describes that chief official.

clue.text: Notice a change in plant

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters

explanation.surface: A gardener spots a difference in a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkshood or wolfsbane, a poisonous flowering herb, is a garden plant by this name.

clue.text: English animal that's not heartless, just exuberant

parts.note: a bull is a male bovine
IE stands for id est, Latin for that is

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter of the word not

explanation.surface: An English beast, kindly by nature, is full of high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' gives IE, the abbreviation for 'that is'; 'heartless' takes the O from NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubbling over with enthusiasm and high spirits, a lively person is effervescent.

clue.text: Tree that's been here longer

definitions.meaning: a shrub or small tree bearing dark berries

explanation.surface: A tree described as an old resident of the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tree with white flowers and berries; also a comparative meaning older or senior.

clue.text: Left without money, needlewomen can produce it

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside

parts.note: quit means left, departed
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Broke and abandoned, seamstresses still turn out their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking: QUIT goes round L.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded bedcover stitched from patchwork is a classic piece of sewing.

clue.text: Springbok, for example, improved by 300% but left out

indicators.note: left out means the letter for left is removed

parts.note: raised by three hundred per cent, an amount becomes four times as much

explanation.surface: A rugby team's score quadruples but one player is dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Springbok' suggests the South African rugby side, but it is the antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: A springbok is an antelope, an animal walking on four legs.

clue.text: Learning to keep front of glass clear, glass you can see through

indicators.note: to keep means the word for learning holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: lore is knowledge or learning

indicators.note: front of picks the opening letter of glass

parts.note: nett means clear, as in clear profit after deductions

explanation.surface: Study keeps a window clean enough to see through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' signals a container: the word for learning holds the rest. 'clear' here is the accounting sense, as in clear profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of spectacles held on a long handle is an eyeglass for viewing.

clue.text: Validate the start of what can be translated as "tsunami'

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so the letters are rearranged
the start of picks the first letter of what

explanation.surface: A translator checks how to render the Japanese word for a great sea wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the start of' gives W, which 'can be translated' rearranges with VALIDATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge sea wave caused by an earthquake is popularly named after the tide.

clue.text: Assistant director at first assigned to wardrobe and locations

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letters of Assistant and director

parts.note: dresses are garments, the contents of a wardrobe

explanation.surface: A film's assistant director is put in charge of costumes and shooting sites.
explanation.definitionFit: Places where people live or can be found, each identified by street and number.

clue.text: A shilling — European currency communist got hold of

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for a shilling, an old British coin
the ecu was a European unit of currency before the euro
red is a common term for a communist

explanation.surface: A communist gets hold of old British and European coins.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated S.
explanation.definitionFit: To have obtained something firmly is to have gained possession.

clue.text: Dreamlike cricket team, lacking a tail-ender, take on a novice

indicators.note: a tail-ender bats last, so the final letter of the team is dropped

parts.note: Surrey is an English county cricket side
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A cricket side missing its last batsman signs up a beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: SURREY, an English county cricket team, loses its last letter, Y; 'tail-ender' is a cricket term for a low-order batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre and unreal like a dream, after the art movement of Dalí.

clue.text: Where shade wanders

indicators.note: wanders tells us the letters of the word shade roam into a new order

explanation.surface: A ghost drifting about the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: A shade is a ghost, and the classical underworld is where ghosts wander.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the underworld is the realm of the dead, home of departed spirits.

clue.text: Set in uproar — a diocese

indicators.note: in says the letters are contained in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bishop's region thrown into turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' is a receiver, a wireless set.
explanation.definitionFit: A wireless receiver is a set, as with a television set.

clue.text: Drank up in bus station

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for drank is read from the bottom

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily

explanation.surface: Someone finishes a drink at the coach terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage where buses are kept and from which they start is a terminus of this kind.

clue.text: Transitional stage for an admiral, perhaps

definitions.text: Transitional stage for an admiral, perhaps

parts.words: Transitional stage for an admiral, perhaps
parts.note: a naval officer seems meant, but the red admiral is a butterfly, whose pupal stage is meant

explanation.surface: A naval officer between ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: The admiral is a butterfly, the red admiral, not a naval rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The pupa of a butterfly, encased while changing from caterpillar to adult.

clue.text: Wear for jockeys and barristers

definitions.meaning: senior barristers, Queen's Counsel, wear gowns of this fabric

explanation.surface: Clothing worn both at the racecourse and in court.
explanation.walkthrough: A barrister made Queen's (King's) Counsel in Britain 'takes silk', wearing a silk gown.
explanation.definitionFit: Jockeys' colours are made of fine fabric; senior counsel are nicknamed for their gowns.

clue.text: Much sought after, you finally took refuge in a tree

indicators.note: took refuge in puts the chosen letter inside the tree

parts.note: a poplar is a tall tree

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of you

explanation.surface: In great demand, you climb up a tree to hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Widely liked and in demand.

clue.text: Confront a viewer

definitions.meaning: to stare at someone aggressively, face to face
the organ of sight in its socket

explanation.surface: Someone squares up to a person watching.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare someone down challengingly; also the organ one sees with.

clue.text: Dying apple tree eventually starts to produce fruit

indicators.note: starts picks the first letters of the four words before it

explanation.surface: An ailing apple tree finally bears fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet brown fruit of a palm.

clue.text: Advantage rarely comes of her behaviour, said Clough

definitions.text: Advantage rarely comes of her behaviour, said Clough

parts.words: Advantage rarely comes of her behaviour, said Clough
parts.note: Arthur Hugh Clough's poem The Latest Decalogue says of breaking one commandment that advantage rarely comes of it

explanation.surface: A Victorian poet warns of the poor rewards of a woman's conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: Clough's satirical Decalogue says 'Do not adultery commit; Advantage rarely comes of it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A married woman who is unfaithful breaks the seventh commandment.
